# llama-harness v0.2.0

This release unifies the first-party Rust workspace, managed runtime, and
TypeScript and Python SDK package identities at `0.2.0`.

## Highlights

- Rust consumers continue to use the eight-crate `llama-harness` facade set with
  explicitly selected features.
- `@llama-harness/sdk` and the matching platform runtime packages use the
  managed child-sidecar protocol. The Python `llama-harness` wheel includes the
  same reviewed platform runtime.
- SDKs offer protocol 1.1 and retain the documented v1.0 fallback. They report
  their package identity in `client_hello`; the child reports its Cargo identity
  in `runtime_hello`.
- Release validation checks Cargo metadata, runtime hello, SDK tests, package
  contents, checksums, and manifest identity before any separate manual upload.
- Adaptive selects supported execution strategies while preserving Direct's
  validation, approval, cancellation, and effect boundaries. Programmatic
  workloads require explicit host configuration and evaluation-based promotion.
- The Ollama adapter accepts IPv6 loopback addresses, including `[::1]`, while
  continuing to reject non-loopback endpoints.

## Model qualification and limits

The opt-in live task suite exercised real tool requests, approvals, dispatch,
state changes, and final answers. The installed Gemma
`gemma4:e4b-it-q4_K_M` passed 60/60 guided samples on Ollama 0.33.3 across
requested Direct and Adaptive. All Adaptive samples actually used Direct.
The measured LFM `lfm2.5-thinking:1.2b-q4_K_M` profile passed 0/60 and remains
unqualified for that task prompt and catalog. No unauthorized, duplicate, or
unintended writes occurred across either model's samples.

A separate bounded Gemma screening passed 120/120 measured samples across
dependent updates and eight independent reads, with an independent audit of
all tool results, approvals, state and final answers. All actual execution was
Direct; the timing measurements do not establish an advanced-strategy benefit.
Discovery and warmup samples are reported separately in the
[benchmark evidence](https://github.com/tyhuang9/llama-harness/blob/main/evals/local-task-agent/benchmark-ollama-2026-09-05.md).

These results qualify a specific synthetic task integration, not general model
reliability. The current Ollama provider does not declare the structured-plan
or strict AST support needed for DAG or Programmatic execution. Keep the
Programmatic promotion list empty and speculation Disabled until their
separate evidence and activation requirements are satisfied. See the
[retained live evidence](https://github.com/tyhuang9/llama-harness/blob/main/evals/local-task-agent/live-ollama-2026-09-05.md)
and the release-readiness assessment for subsequent workload screening.

## Compatibility and upgrade

Update Rust first-party dependency constraints to `0.2.0`. Install TypeScript
or Python SDK packages only with platform runtime artifacts from the same
reviewed release. The sidecar remains private stdin/stdout JSONL; it does not
start a network service, download binaries, or own application tools and policy.

See `docs/migration.md` for migration and rollback boundaries and
`docs/releasing.md` for the manual registry sequence. This checked-in note does
not authorize publishing, tagging, or creating a release by itself.
